cases.sentence: Он видел, что его герой и командир находился совсем в ___ мыслей.
cases.explain: «другом строе» — after the preposition «в», for location or topic.
cases.translation: “Well, is she pretty? Ah, friend—my pink one is delicious; her name is Dunyásha. …” But on glancing at Rostóv’s face Ilyín stopped short. He saw that his hero and commander was following quite a different train of thought.

cases.sentence: Ростов злобно оглянулся на Ильина и, не отвечая ему, ___ направился к деревне.
cases.explain: «быстрыми шагами» — the instrumental marks the means, company, or complement.
cases.translation: Rostóv glanced angrily at Ilyín and without replying strode off with rapid steps to the village.

cases.sentence: Он говорил, что мужики находились в закоснелости, что в настоящую минуту было неблагоразумно противуборствовать им, не имея ___, что не лучше ли бы было послать прежде за командой.
cases.explain: «военной команды» — the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.
cases.translation: “Decision? What decision? Old dotard! …” cried he. “What have you been about? Eh? The peasants are rioting, and you can’t manage them? You’re a traitor yourself! I know you. I’ll flay you all alive! …” And as if afraid of wasting his store of anger, he left Alpátych and went rapidly forward. Alpátych, mastering his offended feelings, kept pace with Rostóv at a gliding gait and continued to impart his views. He said the peasants were obdurate and that at the present moment it would be imprudent to “overresist” them without an armed force, and would it not be better first to send for the military?

cases.sentence: Дрон был того же мнения; но как только он выразил его, так Карп и ___ напали на бывшего старосту.
cases.explain: «другие мужики» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: After the hussars had come to the village and Rostóv had gone to see the princess, a certain confusion and dissension had arisen among the crowd. Some of the peasants said that these new arrivals were Russians and might take it amiss that the mistress was being detained. Dron was of this opinion, but as soon as he expressed it Karp and others attacked their ex-Elder.

cases.sentence: Дрон был того же мнения; но как только он выразил его, так Карп и другие мужики напали на ___.
cases.explain: «бывшего старосту» — after the preposition «на», the accusative marks the direct object of the verb.
cases.translation: After the hussars had come to the village and Rostóv had gone to see the princess, a certain confusion and dissension had arisen among the crowd. Some of the peasants said that these new arrivals were Russians and might take it amiss that the mistress was being detained. Dron was of this opinion, but as soon as he expressed it Karp and others attacked their ex-Elder.

cases.sentence: — Очередь на твоего сына была, а ты небось гладуха своего пожалел, — вдруг быстро заговорил ___, нападая на Дрона, — а моего Ваньку забрил.
cases.explain: «маленький старичок» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: “It was your son’s turn to be conscripted, but no fear! You begrudged your lump of a son,” a little old man suddenly began attacking Dron—“and so they took my Vánka to be shaved for a soldier! But we all have to die.”

cases.sentence: Дрон напротив зашел в ___, и толпа сдвинулась плотнее.
cases.explain: «задние ряды» — after the preposition «в», the accusative marks the direct object of the verb.
cases.translation: The two tall peasants had their say. As soon as Rostóv, followed by Ilyín, Lavrúshka, and Alpátych, came up to the crowd, Karp, thrusting his fingers into his belt and smiling a little, walked to the front. Dron on the contrary retired to the rear and the crowd drew closer together.

cases.sentence: — крикнул Ростов, ___ подойдя к толпе.
cases.explain: «быстрым шагом» — the instrumental marks the means, company, or complement.
cases.translation: “Who is your Elder here? Hey?” shouted Rostóv, coming up to the crowd with quick steps.

cases.sentence: Но не успел он договорить, как шапка слетела с него и голова мотнулась на бок от ___.
cases.explain: «сильного удара» — after the preposition «от», the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.
cases.translation: But before the words were well out of his mouth, his cap flew off and a fierce blow jerked his head to one side.

cases.sentence: — крикнул ___ Ростова.
cases.explain: «полнокровный голос» — the accusative marks the direct object of the verb.
cases.translation: “Caps off, traitors!” shouted Rostóv in a wrathful voice. “Where’s the Elder?” he cried furiously.

cases.sentence: — ___ кричал он.
cases.explain: «неистовым голосом» — the instrumental marks the means, company, or complement.
cases.translation: “Caps off, traitors!” shouted Rostóv in a wrathful voice. “Where’s the Elder?” he cried furiously.

cases.sentence: Дрон Захарыч, вас, — послышались кое-где ___, и шапки стали сниматься с голов.
cases.explain: «торопливо-покорные голоса» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: “The Elder. … He wants the Elder! … Dron Zakhárych, you!” meek and flustered voices here and there were heard calling and caps began to come off their heads.

cases.sentence: Связанных двух мужиков повели на ___.
cases.explain: «барский двор» — after the preposition «на», the accusative marks the direct object of the verb.
cases.translation: The two bound men were led off to the master’s house. The two drunken peasants followed them.

cases.sentence: Через два часа подводы стояли на дворе ___.
cases.explain: «богучаровского дома» — the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.
cases.translation: Two hours later the carts were standing in the courtyard of the Boguchárovo house. The peasants were briskly carrying out the proprietor’s goods and packing them on the carts, and Dron, liberated at Princess Márya’s wish from the cupboard where he had been confined, was standing in the yard directing the men.

cases.sentence: Мужики оживленно выносили и укладывали на подводы ___, и Дрон, по желанию княжны Марьи выпущенный из рундука, куда его заперли, стоя на дворе, распоряжался мужиками.
cases.explain: «господские вещи» — after the preposition «на», the accusative marks the direct object of the verb.
cases.translation: Two hours later the carts were standing in the courtyard of the Boguchárovo house. The peasants were briskly carrying out the proprietor’s goods and packing them on the carts, and Dron, liberated at Princess Márya’s wish from the cupboard where he had been confined, was standing in the yard directing the men.

cases.sentence: — Ты ее так дурно не клади, — говорил один из мужиков, ___ с круглым, улыбающимся лицом, принимая из рук горничной шкатулку.
cases.explain: «высокий человек» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: “Don’t put it in so carelessly,” said one of the peasants, a man with a round smiling face, taking a casket from a housemaid. “You know it has cost money! How can you chuck it in like that or shove it under the cord where it’ll get rubbed? I don’t like that way of doing things. Let it all be done properly, according to rule. Look here, put it under the bast matting and cover it with hay—that’s the way!”

cases.sentence: — Ишь книг-то, книг, — сказал ___, выносивший библиотечные шкапы князя Андрея.
cases.explain: «другой мужик» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: “Eh, books, books!” said another peasant, bringing out Prince Andréy’s library cupboards. “Don’t catch up against it! It’s heavy, lads—solid books.”

cases.sentence: В Янкове, на ___, он простился с нею почтительно, в первый раз позволив себе поцеловать ее руку.
cases.explain: «постоялом дворе» — after the preposition «на», for location or topic.
cases.translation: Unwilling to obtrude himself on the princess, Rostóv did not go back to the house but remained in the village awaiting her departure. When her carriage drove out of the house, he mounted and accompanied her eight miles from Boguchárovo to where the road was occupied by our troops. At the inn at Yankóvo he respectfully took leave of her, for the first time permitting himself to kiss her hand.

cases.sentence: В Янкове, на постоялом дворе, он простился с нею почтительно, в ___ позволив себе поцеловать ее руку.
cases.explain: «первый раз» — after the preposition «в», the accusative marks the direct object of the verb.
cases.translation: Unwilling to obtrude himself on the princess, Rostóv did not go back to the house but remained in the village awaiting her departure. When her carriage drove out of the house, he mounted and accompanied her eight miles from Boguchárovo to where the road was occupied by our troops. At the inn at Yankóvo he respectfully took leave of her, for the first time permitting himself to kiss her hand.

cases.sentence: Прощайте, княжна, желаю вам счастия и утешения, и желаю встретиться с вами при более ___.
cases.explain: «счастливых условиях» — after the preposition «при», for location or topic.
cases.translation: “How can you speak so!” he blushingly replied to Princess Márya’s expressions of gratitude for her deliverance, as she termed what had occurred. “Any police officer would have done as much! If we had had only peasants to fight, we should not have let the enemy come so far,” said he with a sense of shame and wishing to change the subject. “I am only happy to have had the opportunity of making your acquaintance. Goodbye, Princess. I wish you happiness and consolation and hope to meet you again in happier circumstances. If you don’t want to make me blush, please don’t thank me!”

cases.sentence: Когда она простилась с ним и осталась одна, княжна Марья вдруг почувствовала в глазах слезы, и тут уж не в ___ ей представился странный вопрос, любит ли она его?
cases.explain: «первый раз» — after the preposition «в», the accusative marks the direct object of the verb.
cases.translation: When she had taken leave of him and remained alone she suddenly felt her eyes filling with tears, and then not for the first time the strange question presented itself to her: did she love him?

cases.sentence: Когда он вспоминал про нее, ему становилось весело, и когда товарищи, узнав о бывшем с ним приключении в Богучарове, шутили ему, что он, поехав за сеном, подцепил одну из самых ___ в России, Ростов сердился.
cases.explain: «богатых невест» — after the preposition «из», the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.
cases.translation: The impression the princess made on Rostóv was a very agreeable one. To remember her gave him pleasure, and when his comrades, hearing of his adventure at Boguchárovo, rallied him on having gone to look for hay and having picked up one of the wealthiest heiresses in Russia, he grew angry. It made him angry just because the idea of marrying the gentle Princess Márya, who was attractive to him and had an enormous fortune, had against his will more than once entered his head. For himself personally Nikoláy could not wish for a better wife: by marrying her he would make the countess his mother happy, would be able to put his father’s affairs in order, and would even—he felt it—ensure Princess Márya’s happiness.

cases.sentence: Он сердился именно потому, что мысль о женитьбе на приятной для него, кроткой княжне Марье с ___, не раз против его воли приходила ему в голову.
cases.explain: «огромным состоянием» — after the preposition «с», the instrumental marks the means, company, or complement.
cases.translation: The impression the princess made on Rostóv was a very agreeable one. To remember her gave him pleasure, and when his comrades, hearing of his adventure at Boguchárovo, rallied him on having gone to look for hay and having picked up one of the wealthiest heiresses in Russia, he grew angry. It made him angry just because the idea of marrying the gentle Princess Márya, who was attractive to him and had an enormous fortune, had against his will more than once entered his head. For himself personally Nikoláy could not wish for a better wife: by marrying her he would make the countess his mother happy, would be able to put his father’s affairs in order, and would even—he felt it—ensure Princess Márya’s happiness.
